newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Rwanda would welcome home refugees, Kagame says.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda would welcome home refugees, Kagame says.

text.p: The Rwandan Vice President, Major General Paul Kagame, told the United Nations on Tuesday that all remaining Rwandan refugees would be welcome home but they should not disturb the "peace and security" of the country.
Sergio Vieira de Mello, assistant High Commissioner for Refugees, and Kagame, who is also defence minister, issued a joint statement after holding two-day talks in Kigali.

Rwanda and the U.N. refugee agency (UNHCR) agreed to continue to locate the dispersed refugees, repatriate those willing to return, regroup those unwilling to return, "disarm armed elements and separate ex-combatants", the statement said.
"The Vice President assured UNHCR that all remaining refugees were welcome to return but cautioned that those returning should not disturb the peace and security of the country."
Of the 1.1 million Rwandan Hutus who were in camps in eastern Zaire last October after fleeing ethnic slaughter in Rwanda in mid-1994, at least 53,300 remain in six countries.
More than 825,000 have gone home on their own since last November to escape fighting in the renamed Democratic Republic of Congo (formerly Zaire), the UNHCR said.
Some 26,300 Rwandans are known to remain in the Democratic Republic of Congo of President Laurent Kabila -- where 200,000 are missing after reports of massacres, according to UNHCR.
Between 18,000 and 20,000 Rwandans are in the Congo, 3,800 in Central African Republic, 2,500 in Angola and 700 in Malawi.
